items.content_html:
Summary

Adds virtualisation.bootDiskAdditionalSpace option to configure additional disk space beyond the NixOS closure when useBootLoader = true.

Problem

When virtualisation.useBootLoader = true, qemu-vm.nix creates a systemImage via make-disk-image.nix with additionalSpace = "0M" hardcoded. This means the backing disk image is sized exactly to fit the NixOS closure with zero free space.

Consequence: Any runtime writes fail with ENOSPC (no space left on device):

  • NixOS integration tests that write runtime data
  • Container runtimes pulling images (Docker, Podman)
  • Databases writing journals or data files
  • Applications creating logs or temporary files

The existing virtualisation.diskSize only controls the qcow2 overlay size, not the backing systemImage. This distinction is subtle and undocumented, leading users to expect diskSize to control total available space.

Related Context

The pattern of needing configurable disk space is well-established:

  • VirtualBox module exposes virtualisation.virtualbox.guest.baseImageFreeSpace for the same purpose
  • make-disk-image.nix defaults to additionalSpace = "512M", suggesting this headroom is expected—qemu-vm.nix overriding to "0M" appears unintentional

Changes

  • New option: virtualisation.bootDiskAdditionalSpace (type: string, default: "512M")
  • Wiring: Passes configured value to make-disk-image.nix additionalSpace parameter
  • Test: New qemu-vm-bootdisk-space test validating the option works

Test plan

  • Existing nixosTests.systemd-boot.basic passes
  • New nixosTests.qemu-vm-bootdisk-space passes (tests default 512M, custom 1G, minimal 64M configurations)

Notes for reviewers

Behavioral change: Default increases from "0M" to "512M" additional space. This matches make-disk-image.nix's own default and provides reasonable headroom. Users wanting the old behavior can set bootDiskAdditionalSpace = "0M".

Why a new option vs. respecting diskSize? The existing virtualisation.diskSize controls the qcow2 overlay size, not the backing systemImage. Overloading it would conflate two distinct concepts. A dedicated option is clearer and doesn't change overlay behavior.

items.content_html:
The agent's child SSH sessions inherit its cgroup, so any stop of shellhub-agent.service kills the user's shell (and anything it runs) under the default KillMode=control-group. Two paths trigger that stop on nixos-rebuild switch: an explicit restart when the unit's store path changes, and a cascade from Requires=local-fs.target, which NixOS stops on every activation.

Set restartIfChanged = false and replace requires=[local-fs.target] with wants=[local-fs.target] to preserve ordering without the cascade.

Trade-off: the running agent is no longer refreshed automatically; systemctl restart shellhub-agent is needed to pick up a new version.

Description

Follow-up to #445289 (which added the rustnet package). This adds a NixOS module so users get the equivalent of setcap 'cap_net_raw,cap_bpf,cap_perfmon+eip' automatically: enabling the module installs rustnet and configures a security.wrappers entry, allowing any user to run rustnet without sudo.

Direct setcap on the binary is not viable on NixOS because /nix/store is read-only, so the standard pattern is to wrap the binary via security.wrappers, the same approach used by programs.mtr and programs.wireshark.

Capabilities follow rustnet's documented minimum-privilege set:

  • cap_net_raw: raw socket access for read-only, non-promiscuous packet capture.
  • cap_bpf, cap_perfmon: load eBPF programs and attach kprobes for process tracking on Linux 5.8+.

cap_net_admin is intentionally not granted, since rustnet does not require promiscuous mode. rustnet itself drops the elevated capabilities after pcap and eBPF init via its built-in landlock sandbox.

Usage:

programs.rustnet.enable = true;

items.content_html:
Adds a programs.kopia module that installs kopia and optionally wraps each invocation in a transient systemd service, allowing resource limits to be applied.

Backups can saturate IO and CPU; running them at lower priority keeps the system responsive. The wrapper applies to both CLI invocations and subprocesses spawned by kopia-ui
(programs.kopia.ui.enable), which is commonly added to the desktop environment's autostart to let kopia manage its own backup schedule.

Limits are applied via programs.kopia.systemdProperties (any Property=Value accepted by
systemd-run --property=, e.g. Nice=10, IOWeight=50, CPUWeight=50).

To make the wrapper apply to kopia-ui too, the module needs to redirect which kopia binary it spawns. Previously this path was baked in at build time, so any change would trigger a full electron rebuild. This PR switches kopia-ui to read the path from an environment variable instead, letting the module point it at the wrapper without rebuilds.

To verify it's working, launch kopia-ui with systemdProperties set, then inspect the transient unit: systemctl --user show -p Nice kopia-<pid>.service (substituting whichever property you set). You can find the unit name with systemctl --user list-units 'kopia-*'.

For backups scheduled by systemd rather than kopia itself, see #494870

Note for reviewers; I am maintainer of kopia and kopia-ui

cc @nadir-ishiguro

Summary

fwupd ships /etc/grub.d/35_fwupd. The NixOS module symlinks every entry of cfg.package.filesInstalledToEtc into /etc, so this file is installed unconditionally — including under systemd-boot, rEFInd, Limine, etc., where it does nothing.

Gate it on a new services.fwupd.enableGrubHook option defaulting to config.boot.loader.grub.enable. Existing GRUB users see no change; everyone else gets a cleaner /etc.

items.content_html:
Supersedes #507378 at @rhoriguchi's request, implementing the env-var approach we discussed there.

Adds a declarative services.bazarr.settings option that flows through to Bazarr as DYNACONF_* environment variables at startup. Bazarr uses Dynaconf internally, so this leverages its native env-var overlay (env values take precedence over the on-disk config.yaml at load time) instead of introducing a second merge mechanism on top.

Compared with #507378, this drops:

  • The preStart script and pkgs.yaml-merge dependency
  • The mutableSettings option (no longer meaningful: NixOS doesn't write to the config file)
  • The yq-go test dep (no longer needed for assertions)

Two declared defaults differ from upstream: general.auto_update and analytics.enabled both default to false. Documented in the 26.11 release notes. Tested via three subtests covering service smoke, env-var emission, and end-to-end consumption through bazarr's API.

Note: the test VM logs ERROR lines for bazarr's update/announcement checks against Github/jsdelivr. Expected, since the VM has no external network and these checks fail gracefully.

cc @diogotcorreia.
